correctness.rationale: In spin coordinates s_i=2x_i-1, with S_A and S_B the two side sums, the equilibrium condition is delta_i s_i S_B>=0 for i in A and delta_j s_j S_A>=0 for j in B. This follows from the stated payoff difference and leaves both actions feasible at zero opposite sum. With both sums zero there are q(a)q(b) labeled profiles. With S_B=0 but S_A nonzero, B is forced to s_j=delta_j sign(S_A), and its sum vanishes exactly when d_B=0; there are then 2^a-q(a) choices on A. Reversing sides gives the other single-tie contribution. With both sums nonzero they obey S_A=d_A sign(S_B), S_B=d_B sign(S_A), with exactly two sign pairs and corresponding profiles when d_A d_B>0, otherwise none. These independent cases establish the count for all positive sizes, including singletons. Even-even sizes have a double-tie profile for every role assignment; the all-coordinator A/all-anti-coordinator B assignment realizes the minimum in even-even and proves failure of role-robust existence otherwise. Setting both imbalances zero in even-even maximizes the count: the free-part additions are each at least two, whereas the nonzero-imbalance addition is at most two. Under fair independent roles, a side's imbalance vanishes with mass q(t)/2^t and has fair sign when nonzero; this gives the stated probabilities in each parity case.

evidence: Pei–Cao–Zhang covers more than two strategies on a complete bipartite graph with homogeneous opposite roles on the two sides. Specializing to two strategies gives existence iff both sides are even and the balanced-profile count q(a)q(b) for that assignment; it does not cover arbitrary fixed mixed-role compositions.

Arditti et al. give cohesiveness-based existence conditions in the general mixed game. Vanelli et al.'s all-to-all theorem uses threshold equations on a different graph; their broader signed-network theorem guarantees specified partial actions under hypotheses rather than a complete count.

originality.rationale: A distinct indexed record, 7d5cc658885e, contains the same full labeled count for every size and role composition, the same all-role parity and minimum, and the same fair-role probability under complementation. The frozen statement's explicit even-even maximum follows mechanically from that identical count by setting both imbalances to zero. The model and proof correspond under a binary action relabeling and equivalent payoff scaling. There is no uncovered finding in the frozen claim relative to the inspected catalogue. This establishes current equivalent coverage, not chronological priority: the two catalogue dates differ, the matching entry is dated later, and this comparison does not show the November 2 finding was already public elsewhere when it was made or that either record derives from the other.
residual_risks: The indexed exact match is dated November 8 UTC and the frozen record November 2 UTC. Independent discovery order and first-public priority were not established by exact formula comparison or catalogue dates.

value.rationale: The underlying problem is worthwhile: it is a natural complete classification that quantifies the importance of weak ties and role placement. But the frozen package adds no substantive standalone result to the inspected exact census and four-stratum argument. The separately emphasized maximum is direct maximization of the same formula, not a new boundary or independently useful uncovered classification. This is an incremental-value failure under the scientific standard, not a claim that the equilibrium formula is uninteresting or incorrect.
residual_risks: No conclusion about the value of a genuinely different extension, such as nonuniform thresholds or a tie-dependent dynamics, is made.
